item.mechanism: Coherent interfaces of nanoprecipitates facilitate dislocation transmission and relieve stress concentrations, preventing premature crack initiation and maintaining ductility while providing strength.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 (at.%) refractory high-entropy alloy with stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs)
item.operating_conditions: Ambient temperature and 800 °C; tensile deformation up to 14% strain; after stepwise thermo-mechanical processing (cold rolling, annealing at 900 °C, aging at 650 °C)
item.supporting_observation: Dislocations cut through δ-lamellae and are pinned by γ″ particles; shearing of δ-lamellae leads to coherent misalignment rather than microcrack formation at 14% strain.
item.scope_limits: Does not hold for traditional alloys with brittle secondary phases (e.g., silicides, B2, Laves) or intermetallic compounds at grain boundaries which cause embrittlement.
item.alternatives_considered: Single precipitation processes (limited strengthening potency) and non-coherent precipitates (cause brittle fracture).
quotes: The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation.
At a strain of 14%, shearing of the δ-lamellae by the slip bands leads to a large local shear (~40%) (Fig. 4c ), rather than the creation of a crack, which alleviates the local stress concentration.

Unlike traditional W-based heavy alloys where intermetallic compounds invariably act as the origin of microcracks from major dislocation pile-ups during deformation, the coherent interface of the δ phase in the W-based HEA effectively alleviates this problem.

item.mechanism: Precipitation hardening via shearing of ordered δ-lamellae provides strengthening, modeled by the Hall–Petch relationship based on lamellar thickness.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy containing coherent δ-lamellae (D0a structure)
item.operating_conditions: Tensile loading at ambient temperature; δ-lamellae formed by annealing at 900 °C for 5 min; lamellar width ~40 nm.
item.supporting_observation: Dislocations cut through δ-lamellae; modeling estimates ~425 MPa stress required to shear the ordered δ-lamellae.
item.scope_limits: Applicable specifically to the coherent δ-lamellar structure; not stated if incoherent δ phases would follow this mechanism.
item.alternatives_considered: Grain boundary precipitation leading to intergranular embrittlement (avoided by pipe diffusion nucleation).
quotes: Because of its coherent interface, the primary strengthening feature of the δ-lamellae can be deemed to be the hinderance of dislocation motion by the δ/fcc lamellar boundaries.
Based on such modeling, we estimate that a high stress of ~425 MPa is required to shear the ordered δ-lamellae.

item.mechanism: Precipitation hardening via shearing of coherent γ″ particles dominates strengthening, driven by order hardening and lattice misfit due to small size and low misfit.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy containing coherent γ″ particles (D022 structure)
item.operating_conditions: Tensile loading at ambient temperature; γ″ particles formed by aging at 650 °C for 20 h; particle size ~10 nm; lattice misfit ~0.013.
item.supporting_observation: Dislocation motion is pinned by γ″ particles; hardening contribution measured at ~600 MPa.
item.scope_limits: Relies on particles being ~10 nm and maintaining coherent interfaces; not stated for larger or incoherent particles.
item.alternatives_considered: Orowan looping (implied not dominant due to shearing mechanism).
quotes: With respect to the γ ″ phase, as the γ ″ particles were ~10 nm in size and maintained a coherent interface with low lattice misfit (~0.013) throughout the deformation process, strengthening by precipitate shearing was clearly the dominant mechanism.
Order hardening and lattice misfit strengthening can be considered as the main strengthening features of the γ′′ nano-precipitates.
The hardening from the γ′′ can be measured by uniaxial tensile testing to be ~600 MPa (Fig. 3a ).

item.mechanism: Homogeneous distribution of precipitates within grains (rather than at boundaries) prevents intergranular embrittlement and allows for high ductility.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy with δ-lamellae and γ″ particles
item.operating_conditions: Annealing at 900 °C for 5 min followed by aging at 650 °C for 20 h; room temperature tensile testing.
item.supporting_observation: δ-lamellae nucleated at dislocation pile-ups via rapid pipe diffusion, resulting in homogeneous distribution within fcc grains.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the stepwise thermo-mechanical processing used; not tested for other processing routes.
item.alternatives_considered: Precipitation at grain boundaries which leads to intergranular embrittlement in traditional alloys.
quotes: This effect results in the homogeneous distribution of δ-lamellae within the fcc grains, instead of precipitation at grain boundaries that can lead to intergranular embrittlement in traditional alloys.

A major reason for this is the homogeneous distribution of the SCCPs structure, which facilitates the steady accommodation of a large number of dislocations at the coherent δ/matrix interfaces during plastic deformation.
During such processes, owing to rapid pipe diffusion, the δ-lamellae nucleated promptly at dislocation pile-ups when annealed at 900 °C.

item.mechanism: Sluggish grain growth and high thermal stability of coherent precipitates maintain high yield strength at elevated temperatures (up to 800 °C).
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy with SCCPs structure
item.operating_conditions: Elevated temperatures up to 800 °C; annealing at 800 °C for 50 h (δ phase) and 40 h (γ″ phase).
item.supporting_observation: Yield strength above 1 GPa maintained at 800 °C; no substantial change in grain size or precipitate size after long-term annealing at 800 °C.
item.scope_limits: Stability confirmed up to 800 °C; not stated for temperatures significantly higher than 800 °C.
item.alternatives_considered: Instability of high-temperature precipitate phases in nickel-base superalloys.
quotes: Notably, a yield strength above 1 GPa is maintained at temperatures as high as 800 °C due to sluggish grain growth.
Indeed, we examined the stability of this phase at elevated temperatures and found that there was no substantial change in size of the γ ″ particles after aging at 800°C for 40 h.

item.mechanism: Stepwise thermo-mechanical processing enables independent control of two distinct coherent precipitate types (δ and γ″) in different temperature ranges.
item.operating_conditions: Cold rolling, annealing at 900 °C for 5 min (Step I), aging at 650 °C for 20 h (Step II).
item.supporting_observation: δ-lamellae formed at 900 °C; γ″ particles formed at 650 °C; distinct morphologies (lamellar vs. spheroidal) and structures (D0a vs. D022) achieved.
item.scope_limits: Requires specific Ni/Fe ratio (2-4) and 5 at.% Ta addition to avoid μ phase formation.
item.alternatives_considered: Single precipitation process (limited potency) and uncontrolled multiple precipitation leading to brittle intermetallics.
quotes: We construct a sequence of stepwise controllable coherent nanoprecipitations (SCCPs) with distinct nanoscale coherent δ and γ ″ precipitates in different phase-transition temperature ranges.
We first control the Ni/Fe ratio to be between 2 and 4 to avoid the formation of the topologically close-packed μ phase at phase boundaries.

item.mechanism: Synergistic strengthening from two types of nanoscale precipitates contributes to overall high strength (~1 GPa from precipitates alone) without compromising ductility.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy with SCCPs structure
item.operating_conditions: Ambient temperature tensile testing; after full stepwise processing.
item.supporting_observation: Yield strength increased from ~600 MPa (as-cast) to ~2.0 GPa (SCCPs); ductility increased to ~15%.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the combination of δ-lamellae and γ″ particles; not stated for other precipitate combinations.
item.alternatives_considered: Single precipitation mechanisms which provide limited strengthening.
quotes: Hence, the synergistic strengthening of the two types of nanoscale precipitates in the SCCPs structure provides a prime contribution to the overall ~1 GPa strength of the W-based refractory HEA.

With the subsequent γ ″ -strengthen (Step II), the yield strength of the material can be further increased to 2.0 GPa with an ultimate tensile strength of 2.15 GPa without compromising the tensile ductility, which actually increases to ~15%.
The coherent interfaces of SCCPs facilitate the dislocation transmission and relieve the stress concentrations that can lead to premature crack initiation.

item.mechanism: Coherent misalignment of δ-lamellae under high strain reduces the tendency for cleavage fracture.
item.system: (W 1.5 Ni 2.25 Fe) 95 Ta 5 alloy with δ-lamellae
item.operating_conditions: Tensile deformation at ambient temperature; strain > 10%.
item.supporting_observation: At 14% strain, shearing of δ-lamellae leads to coherent misalignments instead of microcrack formation.
item.scope_limits: Dependent on the presence of coherent δ-lamellae; not applicable to incoherent or brittle phases.
item.alternatives_considered: Microcrack formation from dislocation pile-ups in traditional alloys.
quotes: Moreover, the coherent misalignment of δ-lamellae (Fig. 4c ) plays an important role in reducing the tendency for cleavage.
When the strain exceeds 10%, the shearing of δ-lamellae by slip bands leads to coherent misalignments instead of microcrack formation.
At a strain of 14%, shearing of the δ-lamellae by the slip bands leads to a large local shear (~40%) (Fig. 4c ), rather than the creation of a crack, which alleviates the local stress concentration.
